# W0.11 work-volume lane: realized symmetry merges (D6) and the piece-level falsifier (D1(b)) (2026-09-27)

This note is the persisted result of the W0.11 items "Symmetry: count of realized merges" and "Piece-level
falsifier" of `docs/research/fable51_next_push_master_plan_2026-09-27.md` (§4 D1, D6; W0.11). It gives the
D-session a measured, labelled work factor for D6 and D1(b). It does not cover the other W0.11 inputs (G2' and
union-cover bounds, dense cells, hot-owner closure import: census lane W0.7/W0.9; I1b was dropped by addendum 0.1).

Labels: **[M]** measured on saved state or on a run whose directory and binary sha256 are cited; **[M-off]** exact
offline computation on saved state (the question "what would another rule have done" is answered on the saved
trajectory, not by re-running it); **[E]** estimate or interpretation. No campaign was started, stopped, signalled
or written. The v2 gen-7 checkpoint was read from a block clone. No engine code was changed. Tools are on branch
`fable_5_1-v3-wv` under `tools/research/wv/` (README there); raw outputs under `TMP/w0/wv/`.

Both D6 and D1(b) are below the 2x launch-blocking threshold. D1(b) is refuted as a work lever. D6 is not refuted:
it is a moderate domain-volume lever whose net value depends on an admission cost that has not been measured.

## 1. D6: verified automorphisms and the merges they would have realized

### 1.1 The group [M]

`tools/research/wv/family_automorphisms.rs` is a rustred-core example. It builds the five-loop family from
`examples/input/tide_five_loop.toml` through `rustred::input::Compiler` (the application's path). The family
fingerprint matches the saved-owner selection. The example enumerates every loop map whose rows are signed line
momenta and that maps all 15 lines to signed lines: 11,531,520 signed basis images, 16 integer candidates. It
authenticates each candidate with `sector::symmetry::verify` plus `permutation::compile`: 16 verified, 0 rejected.
The candidates give 8 distinct line permutations. `Canonicalizer::try_new` derives a group of order 8, equal to
the candidate set (closed).

- Output: `TMP/w0/wv/sym/group.json`. Binary sha256 in `sym/example.sha256`, stderr in `sym/auts.stderr`.
- Stabilizers of the 67 Apply owner masks: 44 trivial, 18 of order 2, 4 of order 4, 1 of order 8
  (`111010100100101`).
- No two saved owners lie in the same orbit, so D6 cannot merge across Apply owners.
- Route masks: 8,246 masks in the selection. They fall into 2,294 orbits, with 1-8 selected masks per orbit.
- **The hot owner `011101110111000` has a trivial stabilizer.** So does the second-costliest owner,
  `010011111101011`.

### 1.2 Method [M-off]

The standalone `wv` crate reads the CP5 checkpoint with the census decoders (`tools/research/census`,
7d6dd2f1, copied unchanged). The state is a clone of v2 gen 7: 74,156,033 domains, 45,889,639 records and
1,192,281,291 edges.

For every Apply domain Q and every non-identity element s of its owner's stabilizer, the tool asks whether sQ is
contained in an admitted Apply domain of the same owner under four filters:
- **sym_before:** a domain with a smaller ID. This is the realized merge: at Q's admission, a canonicalising
  admission that also tested images would have hit that container.
- **sym_native_before:** a native with a smaller ID.
- **sym_other:** any other domain. This is an upper bound.
- **identity** (s = id): the plain-containment baseline.

Containment is exact. `tight.rs` computes the per-axis, A, R and D extrema of the lattice point set with integer
interval arithmetic. Q ⊆ C holds iff every defining inequality of C holds at the matching extremum of Q. Unit
tests compare this against brute-force enumeration. A static k-d tree over 34-component container keys answers
the dominance queries (unit test against a linear scan).

Checks:
- identity_before = 0 on all 19,366,066 Apply domains. This is as it must be: the engine already aliases plain
  containment in an earlier admitted domain.
- A 4,000-pair audit used the census predicate `geom::contains_point` over `geom::enumerate`, which is
  independent of `tight.rs`. It found 763 positives, 760 verified pointwise, 0 violations and 3 skipped over the
  point cap. All 2,818 negatives were confirmed, and the tree agreed with a linear scan on 4,000/4,000
  (`sym/gen7-sym-route-audit.json`).
- The Apply pass was run twice with identical results (27,727,244 containment queries each; `gen7-sym-apply.json`,
  `gen7-sym-apply-v3.json`). Wall 528 s and 300 s, peak RSS 15-17 GB.

### 1.3 Apply: realized merges [M-off]

Seconds are v2 record seconds. "Pending seconds" are predicted per (phase, owner, half-decade of points) binned
mean [E].

| Set | Apply domains | natives | native s | pending Apply | pending native s [E] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| total (gen 7) | 19,366,066 | 5,949,328 | 241,443 | 8,751,708 | 121,295 |
| sym_before (direct) | 1,536,487 (7.93%) | 364,449 (6.13%) | 6,151 (2.55%) | 705,808 (8.06%) | 3,297 (2.72%) |
| sym_native_before | 1,304,144 (6.73%) | 354,617 (5.96%) | 5,949 (2.46%) | | |
| direct + cascade (below) | 1,695,332 (8.75%) | 392,956 (6.61%) | 6,355 (2.63%) | 795,914 (9.09%) | 3,999 (3.30%) |
| sym_other (upper bound) | 2,733,361 (14.1%) | 762,953 (12.8%) | 13,712 (5.68%) | 938,520 (10.7%) | 4,241 (3.50%) |

**Cascade.** A merged domain gets no ID, no ledger obligation and no out-edges. A node is then also avoided once
every one of its in-edge sources is avoided. This is a least fixpoint over the saved edges, with the 67-ID
protected prefix excluded (`wv volume`, `sym/gen7-volume-apply-only.json`).
- It adds 158,845 Apply domains and 1,189,926 Route domains (2.17% of Route).
- In total that is 3.89% of all domains and 4.11% of edges.
- Caveat: it does not model the unexplored future of pending domains, nor containers that the cascade itself
  would remove. It is a first-order estimate on the saved trajectory [E].

**Owner classes (addendum 0.1 item 7).**
- The 23 owners with a nontrivial stabilizer hold 7,807,170 Apply domains and 35,013 native seconds (14.5% of
  Apply native seconds).
- Inside that class, sym_before is 19.7% of domains and 17.6% of native seconds. This reproduces the physics lens's
  −20.5% Apply domains, but only for this class.
- The lens figure does not carry to the whole walk, because the class excludes the hot owner (154,805 s, 64.1%)
  and 43 other owners.
- The biggest contributors are `111001100111001` (18.9% of its domains, 2,180 s) and `110110111101001` (17.4%,
  1,685 s).

**Stability.** The direct share is flat across generations: 7.8%, 8.0%, 7.6%, 9.0% and 6.8% of the Apply
domains discovered in generations 3-7. It does not grow with the walk.

**Work factor [E].** Committed plus predicted pending Apply seconds are 362,738 s. The avoided seconds are
9,448 s direct and 10,354 s with the cascade, i.e. 2.6-2.9%, a **1.03x** factor.

The admission-side cost is not included. The lookup counts are [M-off]; their cost was not measured:
- Apply: 1.43 lookups per Apply domain on average (the identity plus 0.43 images), against 1 today. On C-5F: 1.35.
- Route: an image may land in another Route mask, so a Route admission tests every family element whose image mask
  is selected. Over the 8,246 selected Route masks, that is 1 to 8 lookups, 5.52 on average (unweighted by
  domains; from `group.json` and `route_masks.txt`).

The admission stage is already the coordinator's bottleneck in the legacy engine (ordered_commit 51.4% of
coordinator wall in v2). The epoch design projects 18-47% admission share at 1G domains (addendum 0.1 item 8). The
net effect of D6 on wall time can therefore be negative or positive; it cannot be decided from these counts [E].
A hit also saves the domain's ID, ledger obligation, index entry and out-edges, which the lookup count does not
reflect.

### 1.4 Route [M-off]

Route buckets are masks, so every family element is tried, not only the stabilizer. An image may land in another
mask's tree. The pass covered all 54,789,967 Route domains in 7,973 mask buckets (no sampling), in 277 s wall with
a peak RSS of 17 GB (`sym/gen7-sym-route-all.json`, `gen7-flags-route.bin`).

| Set | Route domains | natives | native s | pending Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| total (gen 7) | 54,789,967 | 21,516,094 | 1,951 | 19,514,686 |
| sym_before (direct) | 9,194,071 (16.78%) | 3,465,938 (16.1%) | 288 (14.8%) | 2,829,104 (14.5%) |
| sym_before, first hit in another mask | 7,894,786 (14.41%) | | | |
| sym_other (upper bound) | 13,429,973 (24.5%) | 5,171,826 (24.0%) | 410 (21.0%) | 3,291,285 (16.9%) |

- identity_before is 0 again, as for Apply.
- The 1M-draw sample run earlier (`gen7-sym-route-audit.json`) gave 16.79% and 14.42%, which agrees.

**Both phases with the cascade** (`sym/gen7-volume.json`):
- 11,474,418 domains avoided, 15.5% of all 74,156,033: 1,713,041 Apply and 9,761,377 Route.
- 10.5% of edges and 14.7% of natives.
- Of the pending domains: 13.8%.
- Native seconds avoided: 6,528 Apply + 304 Route = 6,832 of 243,394 (2.8%).
- Predicted pending seconds avoided [E]: 4,265 Apply + 146 Route = 4,411 of 122,393 (3.6%).

**Reading [E].**
- D6 is a domain-volume lever of about 1.18x fewer domains and 1.16x fewer pending domains on gen 7 (Route alone
  1.20x, 1.22x with the cascade). The domain figure happens to match the physics lens's 1.21x route masks.
- On the gen-7 cost mix it is a ~1.03x CPU lever.
- Revision 1 discounted the Route part as overlapping the I2 route-witness lever. I2 as built increases total C-5F
  work and is not shipped (orchestrator decision 3), so no discount applies. If a rebuilt I2 (open item D-I2) ships,
  the overlap should be measured then.

### 1.5 What D6 would need if it were signed off anyway [E]

- A certification rule. A root certifies through a σ-image container, and the oracles must learn the rule:
  I(n) = I(σn) holds for every point, and it is proved by the verified permutation. Neither oracle checks this
  today.
- Admission-side image queries. A Route admission needs up to 8 lookups (5.5 on average over the selected masks,
  unweighted), because images move across masks.
- Digest binding of the group (`group.json` element list) into the checkpoint.

On CPU, the measured benefit is small on the gen-7 cost mix: 1.03x on Apply, and the hot owner is untouched. On
domain volume it is about 1.18x, which is not small next to the other measured domain-volume lever (§1.6). Whether it
pays depends on the admission cost, which can only be measured once the epoch admission path exists (W2).

### 1.6 Same-control comparison with the G2' falsifier (added in revision 2)

Orchestrator decision 7 promoted G2' as "the only measured domain-volume lever": scheduled domains 0.79-0.80x in
its union arm "u". The D6 figures above are on another basis. They are offline on the saved gen-7 trajectory, and

off-arm checkpoint.

- The same `wv-bin4` (sha256 `8da0c5ec…`) and `group.json` as gen 7 (script `TMP/w0/wv/c5f/run_c5f.sh`).
- Outputs: `c5f-sym-apply.json`, `c5f-sym-route-all.json`, `c5f-volume.json` and `c5f-volume-apply-only.json`.
- Audit (`c5f-sym-route-audit.json`): 4,000 pairs; 1,235 positives, all verified pointwise, 0 violations; 2,752

| C-5F Ordered W24 | domains | natives | edges | native s | basis |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| D6, Apply direct | 10.65% of Apply | 9.89% of Apply | | 8.40% of Apply | [M-off] |
| D6, Route direct | 10.30% of Route (4.18% first hit in another mask) | 9.09% of Route | | 7.46% of Route | [M-off] |

G2' figures: `TMP/w0/g2falsify/gate-table-2.md`, binary 461dbd84.

Reading [E]:
- On domain volume, D6 is of the same order as G2': 0.884x against 0.802x (arm u) and 0.877x (arm n) on the same
  control. The bases differ. D6 is counted offline on one saved trajectory, and a canonicalising run would take a
  different one. G2' is measured on live runs. The two levers are not additive, and their overlap was not measured.
- On CPU they are far apart: D6 saves 8.8% of native seconds on C-5F and 2.8% on gen 7, while G2' arm u halves the
  inspector seconds. That CPU gap, not domain volume, is what separates the two levers.
- C-5F inverts the gen-7 cost mix (addendum 0.1 item 7). C-5F has 13 Apply owners. The 4 of them with a nontrivial
  stabilizer (order 2) hold 46.5% of C-5F Apply native seconds; on gen 7 the 23 such owners hold 14.5%. The hot owner
  holds 1.0% on C-5F against 64% on gen 7. That is why D6's CPU share is higher on C-5F. For a campaign that resumes
  from an aged state, the gen-7 mix is closer to what matters [E].

## 2. D1(b): does a physics root certify at piece granularity?

### 2.1 Set-up [M]

The four-loop controls are FG, BMW, H and X, run with their historical command lines (`run_variant.py`):
- binary `TMP/fable51-controls/bin/rustred-4a17f9c7` (sha256 `4a17f9c7…b395e`), W6, Ordered, 900 s cap;
- lane CPUs 72-87, 328-343, in four slots of 4+4 CPUs; the foreign load on each slot is recorded in
  `metrics.json` (0.04-0.80);
- query variants from `make_piece_queries.py` (`TMP/w0/wv/pieces/queries`, SHA256SUMS). Physics queries are
  verbatim. Each owner's helper is replaced by the listed pieces, helper-first.

Every run was checked by:
- the Python audit (oracle branch);
- `walk-verify-closure` with full F10 re-inspection (`TMP/w0/oracle/bin/rustred-f4d1870f`, sha256 `f4d1870f…b2f4`).
  It passes `--require-closure` whenever the engine reports 0 frontiers and a drained worklist. Every one of the
  33 verifier reports is PASS, and independently_verified equals certified for every physics count below;
- `piece_cones.py`: reverse reachability from frontier, error and uninspected nodes over the CP5 edges.

Batch: `TMP/w0/wv/pieces/runs/b1`. Table: `TMP/w0/wv/pieces/b1-summary.json`.

### 2.2 The legacy engine cannot keep nested pieces apart [M]

- `walking/initial_orthants.rs` keeps one fast-path orthant per (phase, owner): the full orthant with the largest
  rank bound, where "unbounded" wins.
- Ordinary containment returns the minimum-ID live container.

Measured consequence: in the `shells` variant (rank ≤12, ≤14, ≤16, unbounded) and the `aslabs` variant (A ≤19, ≤25,
unbounded), every dependency edge lands on the unbounded top piece. Inner pieces get 0 in-edges in all 9 runs (`shells`, BMW `shellsk`, `aslabs`),
and physics certification is identical to `unbounded`. So D1(b) can only be tested literally at whole-helper
granularity, or offline (§2.4).

### 2.3 Measured runs [M]

Natives, frontiers and certified physics roots (independently verified / total):

| Variant | FG | BMW | H | X | Sum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (today's helpers: rank-12 orthant; BMW upstream A≤19) | 98,627 nat, 0 fr, 124/124 | 146,850, 0, 134/134 | 24,247, 0, 314/314 | 46,498, 0, 328/328 | 316,222 natives, 234.6 native s, **900/900** |
| unbounded helpers (the D1(b) shape) | 124, 85 fr, 60/124 | 134, 138, 46/134 | 314, 258, 90/314 | 328, 556, 10/328 | 900 natives, **206/900 (22.9%)** |
| shells / aslabs (nested, one walk) | 60/124 | 46/134 | 90/314 | 10/328 | = unbounded (collapse) |
| r12aslabs: rank-12 orthant + A-slabs, no unbounded top (stopped at 900 s) | 1.73M nat, 0.47M pending, 255 fr, 85/124 | 2.63M, 0.90M, 522, 111/134 | 3.08M, 0.78M, 1,447, 196/314 | 1.66M, 0.40M, 3,112, 248/328 | 9.10M natives (29x base), not drained, 640/900 |
| rank14 / rank16 / rank20 (one piece, A as base) | 110k / 169k / 296k | 267k / 469k / 1.17M | 31k / 62k / 65k | 54k / 116k / 99k | all drained, 0 frontiers, 900/900 each |

- The −71%-node counterfactual of the physics lens is real in node count: unbounded helpers use 900 natives
  against 316,222. But it comes with 694 of 900 physics roots uncertified.
- Keeping A-slab pieces apart is possible in the legacy engine, because min-ID containment resolves pieces that
  carry an A bound. It does not drain, it produces up to 3,112 frontiers, and it certifies fewer roots than the
  base at 29x its natives.
- Larger rank pieces cost more, not less. rank20 needs 5.2x the base natives in total, because a rank-r helper
  emits escapes up to rank r+2.

### 2.4 The idealized piece-aware rule, composed offline [M-off]

`piece_graph.py` builds the piece graph from the drained single-piece runs at rank levels 12, 14, 16 and 20 (BMW:
the `k` variants that keep its A≤19 bounds) and the unbounded top run T.
- A piece S(o, r) has an edge to S(o', r) when the helper of o reaches the helper of o' in run r through nodes of
  rank ≤ r.
- It has an edge to S(o', r_j) for every escape node (rank bound > r) of owner o', with r_j the smallest level ≥
  the escape's rank bound, or T if there is none.
- T(o) is bad iff the top run's helper of o is not closed.
- A level piece is bad iff its own run left a frontier, error or pending node in its cone. None is: every level
  run drained with 0 frontiers.
- A root certifies iff its rank-12 piece reaches no bad piece.

Output: `TMP/w0/wv/pieces/compose/*.json`.

| Levels | FG | BMW | H | X | Certified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 + T | 86 | 112 | 193 | 248 | 639/900 (71.0%) |
| 12, 14 + T | 106 | 124 | 241 | 267 | 738/900 (82.0%) |
| 12, 14, 16 + T | 122 | 134 | 298 | 328 | 882/900 (98.0%) |
| 12, 14, 16, 20 + T | 124 | 134 | 312 | 328 | 898/900 (99.8%) |

**Work of the idealized rule.** Each reached piece counts as one whole-region inspection, measured by its helper
record's seconds in its own run. For BMW, the non-escape natives inside pieces are added, counted once per piece
that traverses them, which is an upper bound. At levels 12-20 the totals are:

| Family | Piece rule (s) | Base run (s) | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| FG | 22.5 | 38.5 | 0.58x |
| BMW | 93.8 | 73.7 | 1.27x |
| H | 81.1 | 38.7 | 2.10x |
| X | 170.1 | 83.8 | 2.03x |
| Sum | 367.4 | 234.6 | **1.57x** |

These are single-run native seconds under a 0.04-0.80 foreign load, so each ratio carries a noise band of roughly
±30% [E].

**Reading.**
- Physics roots do certify at a fine enough piece granularity (898/900).
- But the pieces that carry the certification are the bounded rank-≤20 helpers.
- Each of those helpers drains and certifies 900/900 by itself, with 0 frontiers.
- At levels 12-20, only 2 roots (both H) reach the unbounded top piece T, and they are exactly the 2 uncertified
  ones.

So on the four-loop, D1(b) reduces to option (a) (bounded helpers) plus an unbounded top that nothing needs, and it
costs more work.

**Five-loop caveat [E].** The four-loop controls drain with rank-12 helpers. The five-loop campaign has bounded
helpers that did not drain in the interim, so the regime differs. The falsifier shows the mechanism (collapse,
frontier spread through unbounded helpers, cost of rank escalation), not a five-loop work number. A five-loop
version would need the same composition over five-loop level runs, which are not ≤1 h runs.

## 4. Limits

- D6 is measured offline on two saved trajectories: v2 gen 7 and one C-5F Ordered control. A canonicalising run
  would take a different trajectory. The flat per-generation share on gen 7 suggests the order of magnitude holds
  [E]. The cascade is a first-order least fixpoint. No canonicalising run was made, so D6 has no live measurement,
  unlike G2'.
- The admission cost of D6 (image lookups on the admission path) was not measured; only lookup counts were.
- The Route part covers realized hits only. Route natives are <1% of native seconds on gen 7, so Route bears on
  domain and pending volume, memory and index size, not CPU.
- The D1(b) runs are single repeats under foreign load.
- The four-all variant files exist (`queries/four-all-*.json`) but were not run. Per addendum 0.1 item 7, four-all
  is an addition, not a replacement for the per-family controls.
